items.text:
MANSFIELD, Texas -- United States women's national team head coach Emma Hayes said she expects El Salvador to play "the game of their lives" in Friday's Concacaf W Championship quarterfinal.
The winner will automatically qualify for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil.
"I always respect every opponent, and you have to start with that," Hayes told reporters on Thursday at Texas Health Mansfield Stadium. "I think if you start looking at things like rankings, then you prime your brain to say things like, 'Oh, it's going to be an easy game.'
"More often than not, from my experiences, they end up being more challenging for lots of reasons. First of all, for El Salvador, this is going to be the game of their lives. They get the opportunity to qualify for the World Cup."
El Salvador are ranked No. 78 in the world and making their first appearance at the Concacaf W Championship after winning their pre-qualifying group.
The United States has qualified for all nine previous Women's World Cups and won four of them, more than any other country. The Americans are ranked second in the world behind Spain and are one of the contenders to win the 2027 edition. They are also the reigning Olympic champions.
"They have a lot of pride, and they want to perform for their country," Hayes said about El Salvador. "There's something at stake, and because of that, it's not a friendly game. And disrupting a team like the United States it might not be going toe-to-toe with us in certain parts of the game, but making it difficult for us? One hundred percent I think that will be the case."
Hayes praised El Salvador's ability to create opportunities in counterattacks and one-v-one opportunities. She also pointed to El Salvador's threat on set pieces.
Earlier in the day at training, U.S. captain Lindsey Heaps told ESPN and a small group of reporters that there is more game footage of Concacaf opponents than in previous cycles, which allows for more specific preparation.
Heaps echoed Hayes, saying that "we do not take any of these games lightly," and that the team prepared for El Salvador like they did for matches against world No. 1 Spain last month.
U.S. forward Sophia Wilson said that each game is like a final, which is good preparation for the World Cup.
"Any Concacaf tournament, we know it's going to be a challenge in a different way," Wilson said. "It's going to be maybe a little bit of a chaotic game, but I think that's a good test for us."
Hayes told reporters at Saturday's NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., that she was excited to finally have the opportunity to start the self-proclaimed "Triple Espresso" of Wilson, Trinity Rodman and Mallory Swanson together for the first time since the 2024 Olympics.
About an hour later, in the opening minutes of the Washington Spirit's 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current, Rodman was tackled hard and injured her shoulder.
Rodman stayed in the match and scored the Spirit's lone goal in second-half stoppage time. She said after the game that her shoulder felt "phenomenal," but U.S. Soccer announced earlier this week that Rodman would miss World Cup qualifying. She was replaced on the roster by forward Jaedyn Shaw.
"For Trin, she took a pretty hard hit," Hayes said on Thursday. "She was pretty beat up after the game. This happens, and unfortunately, she's not fit for this camp, but I'm sure she will be back by January."
Also absent from the U.S. roster is forward and attacking midfielder Pietra Tordin, who earned her first call-up and first cap last month against Spain. Tordin is training with Brazil in Japan during this international window. She holds dual citizenship with the U.S. and Brazil and has played for both countries at the youth international level.
"She was with us, and obviously she's got Brazilian heritage.," Hayes said. "She's going to train with Brazil. No more than that, so she's not cap-tied. I understand. It was a conversation that I've had, particularly with her agent, and yeah, there's no more to be said on it."
El Salvador's federation announced earlier this week that it would pay the players a $1 million shared bonus if they qualify for the World Cup for the first time.
The losers of the four Concacaf quarterfinals will get second chances at qualification in play-in games next week. The two winners of those matches will advance to next year's FIFA global playoff, where the final World Cup berths will be secured.
"Process is a really, really, really heavy word," El Salvador head coach Erick Acuña told reporters on Friday. "We are just trying to go step by step. And every step that we made, we have to be really secure. But we don't want to dream; we want to do.
"At the end of everything, we have to believe in step by step, because I don't want to be lucky. I just want to be secure that we are going to be in these stages all the time, and the only way to do it is believe. We have to believe in our process but inside of the process, there's a lot of things that we have to do. We have to invest. Without investment, there is no progression."

items.title: Bournemouth set new English record in Europe with 5th straight win
items.summary:
Bournemouth's dream Europa League start continued on Thursday as the south-coast club set a new record for a debuting English club in Europe.
Marco Rose's side fought back from a goal down in Spain against Celta Vigo to win 2-1 and extend their perfect start to the competition to five games.
- Europ
items.text:
Bournemouth's dream Europa League start continued on Thursday as the south-coast club set a new record for a debuting English club in Europe.
Marco Rose's side fought back from a goal down in Spain against Celta Vigo to win 2-1 and extend their perfect start to the competition to five games.
- Europa League game halted amid police clashes over fans' Palestine banner
They are the first English club in history to win their first five European games and are only the third team ever in major European competitions to achieve that feat, after Nürnberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73.
It was also a club-record extending 10th straight win in all competitions for Marco Rose's side, who sit an impressive fifth in the Premier League.
Thursday's win, which keeps them top of the Europa League league phase table, was made all the more impressive by the fact it came after playing for more than an hour with 10 men following Bafodé Diakité's red card in the 23rd minute.
"We showed a lot of character," Bournemouth's Amine Adli TNT Sport. "It's amazing to come back in this way and go back home with the three points.
"I think it was down to the mentality of the players. From the moment we conceded the goal, and even after the red card, we always believed in ourselves.
"What's fantastic is that in the dressing room, even before the coach started speaking, everybody was saying, 'we can do this.' Everyone was motivated and still believed we could turn things around."
Adli's cross shortly after time set up Álvaro Rodríguez to head an equalising goal, turning the tables on Celta after they had gone in at halftime a goal up and a man up.
"I was looking for someone in the box," Adli added. "I know Alvaro is very good in the air and he was in a good position so I just tried to deliver a dangerous ball towards the far post."
The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Diakité was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle.
Rodríguez's goal then set the tone for an excellent second half in which Rose's team were comfortably the better side despite their numerical disadvantage.
Substitute Rayan swept in the winner 12 minutes from time to give Bournemouth one foot into the knockout rounds.
Information from ESPN Global Research and PA contributed to this report.

items.title: Kimmich slams 'not Bayern-like' treatment of Musiala amid health row
items.summary:
Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's "not Bayern-like" treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.
Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused
items.text:
Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's "not Bayern-like" treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.
Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in preseason games, drawing protests from players' union FIFPRO.
Now a key player has spoken out, too, and warned Bayern risks undermining its family image.
"What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public," Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday.
"It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either."
Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's run of injuries over the last two years, including a badly fractured leg at the Club World Cup last year, had more impact on his game than the neurological condition.
"It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself," Kimmich added.
Bayern met with Musiala's agents Tuesday and clarified the timeline of events, dismissing speculation Musiala could have concealed the condition when he signed his last contract extension.
Bayern said the club and Musiala's representatives both accept he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after the contract extension.
"This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared," Bayern said.
Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the field in two preseason games, leaving players and fans alarmed.
- Bayern Munich, Jamal Musiala mess shows German champs at their worst
- Bayern Munich: Jamal Musiala's health 'top priority' amid contract doubts
- Injury-hit Bayern beaten by Lille to suffer first UCL loss
Bayern coach Vincent Kompany said at the time the incidents were triggered by a change in the medication Musiala was taking. Musiala was rested for the start of the season and has since missed several games with a muscle issue.
Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Bayern's loss at Lille, which continued a bad week for Bayern.
Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern have lost the lead in the Bundesliga to Borussia Dortmund and have now slipped to 15th in the Champions League standings.

items.title: Europa League game halted amid police clashes over fans' Palestine banner
items.summary:
BATUMI, Georgia -- The UEFA Europa League game between Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva was suspended for around 30 minutes on Thursday when police clashed with fans of the Turkish club after they displayed a banner in support of Palestinians.
The game, being played on neutral ground in Batu
items.text:
BATUMI, Georgia -- The UEFA Europa League game between Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva was suspended for around 30 minutes on Thursday when police clashed with fans of the Turkish club after they displayed a banner in support of Palestinians.
The game, being played on neutral ground in Batumi, Georgia, was halted in the 26th minute but restarted after the interruption and was eventually won 2-1 by Besiktas.
Turkey's Haberturk broadcaster said Georgian police used pepper spray against the Besiktas fans, who also unfurled a Palestinian flag, prompting the referee to stop the game with the score 0-0.
In a statement, Besiktas accused the Georgian security forces of using "disproportionate" force against supporters before and during the game.
"We strongly condemn the security forces for their use of disproportionate force against our fans," the club said. "We also extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to all our fans affected by these incidents."
The Turkish Football Federation condemned the treatment of Besiktas supporters on X, saying they were subjected to unacceptable behavior and discrimination. It said it would press for an investigation.
Earlier, the Besiktas players refused to shake hands with their Hapoel counterparts, the state-run Anadolu Agency reported.
UEFA relocated the match after Turkish authorities said Istanbul could not host it for safety and security reasons.
Unlike two previous Hapoel away games, spectators were allowed in the stadium.

items.title: Thanksgiving delight: USMNT star Pulisic nets vital Milan winner
items.summary:
Christian Pulisic enjoyed a Thanksgiving to remember as the United States star came off the bench to help fuel AC Milan's 4-2 comeback win at Olympiacos in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday.
Despite Milan coach Ruben Amorim describing Pulisic in recent days as the one player his side could not repl
items.text:
Christian Pulisic enjoyed a Thanksgiving to remember as the United States star came off the bench to help fuel AC Milan's 4-2 comeback win at Olympiacos in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday.
Despite Milan coach Ruben Amorim describing Pulisic in recent days as the one player his side could not replace, the attacker was named among the substitutes for the game in Greece.
With Milan trailing 1-0 at halftime, Amorim turned to Pulisic in an attempt to spark a second-half revival. The 28-year-old delivered, volleying home a cross in the 71st minute for the eventual game winner.
As the home side chased an equalizer in the dying moments, Pulisic then laid on a simple fourth goal for Diego Moreira.
"It was a decisive game for us," Pulisic told Sky Sport Italia. "From today, every game is like a final. We didn't start well but we were much better in the second half. It's important to find this intensity."
Goals from Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cissè had earlier brought Milan level after an own goal from Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan and a goal from Jota Silva had put Olympiacos in front 2-0.
Pulisic, who scored in both legs of the U.S. men's national team's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal win over Haiti earlier this month, has now scored in his past five games for club and country. That streak is tied for the best of Pulisic's career, matching his run in September 2024.
After Milan lost three of their first four games in this season's Europa League, Thursday's win could prove vital to their hopes of advancing to the knockout stage.
"It changed our future," Amorim said. "It's completely different to win this game or lose this game. We did well in the second half but we [made] a lot of mistakes again."
Following a low-key start at the Stadio Georgios Karaiskakis, Olympiacos broke the deadlock from a corner in the 31st minute.
Former Inter defender Lorenzo Pirola crashed a header against the crossbar and the ball bounced back into the net off Maignan's arm.
Olympiacos, who were unbeaten in Europe with three wins, scored again four minutes into the second half.
Remo Freuler found Jota Silva at the edge of the penalty area and Silva fired the ball past Maignan into the top corner.
Milan got themselves back into the match through a fine individual goal from Hutchinson in the 56th minute.
The on-loan Nottingham Forest winger picked the ball up on the halfway line and burst down the right before cutting inside at the edge of the penalty area and rolling the ball into the far corner.
The Rossoneri struck again in the 63rd minute, when Hutchinson sent over a cross from the right toward the back post, where Cissè nodded the ball past Olympiacos keeper Stefan Ortega.
Pulisic completed the turnaround with 20 minutes left when he volleyed home a cross from the right after more quick footwork from Hutchinson.
Moreira swept home a fourth in added time following a swift counterattack by Pulisic.
Information from PA contributed to this report.

items.title: USWNT's Coffey grateful for 'surreal' return for Women's World Cup qualifying
items.summary:
DALLAS -- Midfielder Sam Coffey said it is "surreal" to return to the United States women's national team for World Cup qualifying after missing recent major matches due to injuries.
Coffey is back with the U.S. for the first time since April after undergoing a minor knee procedure in May. She said
items.text:
DALLAS -- Midfielder Sam Coffey said it is "surreal" to return to the United States women's national team for World Cup qualifying after missing recent major matches due to injuries.
Coffey is back with the U.S. for the first time since April after undergoing a minor knee procedure in May. She said that the time she missed made her even more grateful to be part of the USWNT.
"I try to never take this environment for granted," Coffey told ESPN and a small group of reporters at training on Thursday. "I feel like that has multiplied now since going through a few injuries this year after not really experiencing that in my career thus far.
"I always have such gratitude for being here, and I think that just is even more so true now. It feels so good to be back and to be able to be here at this time, too, where it's such an important camp and the stakes are really big."
The U.S. plays El Salvador on Friday night in Mansfield, Texas, in the quarterfinals of the Concacaf W Championship. The winner of the match automatically qualifies for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil.
The U.S. women have won four World Cups and never missed the final tournament in nine all-time editions.
Coffey was a spectator from TV for the United States' pair of away games against Brazil in June. Brazil and the U.S. split those results in physical, contentious matches.
Coffey also missed last month's friendly matches against world No. 1 Spain. She was on hand in the stadium for the second match in which the Americans rallied from 2-0 down to earn a 2-2 draw.
"It's always just a privilege and a joy to be here," Coffey said. "I think this year taught me so much about -- so many lessons in that. How much of a gift it is just to be playing and to be playing with the best team in the world, and how much I hated with all my heart missing those windows and being and home and not being able to contribute and be there with the girls.
"I think I just come in with a different perspective now, a bit of a reframe and a re-shift."
Coffey said she is "finding [her] rhythm" again in camp with the team in order to rebuild connections and pick up certain information from the coaching staff. She last played for the U.S. in April against Japan.
Coffey has made 46 career appearances for the USWNT and became an anchor for the team as a defensive midfielder in recent years, including starting during the team's run to a 2024 Olympic gold medal.
Being exposed to different styles of play in England, where she plays for Manchester City, has helped her game, Coffey said.
She added that her knee feels good and she feels physically healthy -- other than a small cold she caught recently.
Coffey was originally named to the USWNT's roster for the October matches against Spain but withdrew from camp after sustaining an ankle injury while playing for Manchester City.
She flew to the U.S. during the international window and watched the U.S. play Spain in Chester, Pennsylvania. What Coffey saw from the team was encouraging, she said.
"It just made me so excited and proud to see how we've progressed and just how good we are, and how we still have like those little last details that we need to fine-tune," Coffey said.

items.title: Europa League: Bournemouth make it a perfect 10 while Celtic leave it late
items.summary:
Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo.
It was a remarkable 10th victory in succession in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for t
items.text:
Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo.
It was a remarkable 10th victory in succession in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time.
The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Bafodé Diakité was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle.
Bournemouth might have folded then, but instead they came roaring back, Álvaro Rodríguez heading them level almost immediately after the start of the second half. A draw would have been an excellent result in the circumstances. Substitute Rayan had other ideas, waiting at the end of a rapid breakaway to sweep in the winner 12 minutes from time. Rose’s team could secure a top-eight finish and a last-16 berth when they host Viktoria Plzen, 4-0 winners over Benfica, in two weeks’ time.
Camilo Durán came to Celtic’s rescue in Europe again after coming off the bench to head a late winner against Torreense in Portugal.
The Colombian striker peeled off to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest and send a downward header into the net in the 85th minute. Durán’s 15th goal of the season earned a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and put Celtic on six points in the Europa League after his double off the bench inspired a comeback win over Besiktas last time out.
Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vázquez sliced Jota’s cross into his own net with Yang Hyun-jun right behind him. But the Portuguese Cup winners levelled 10 minutes later after some sloppy defending. Both Kieran Tierney and Colby Donovan had chances to deal with bouncing balls after Álex Alfaro hit the bar from 22 yards but they could not clear and Haiti international Dany Jean volleyed home.
Celtic dominated second-half possession but clear chances were at a premium until Durán struck. Torreense sit 13th in the Portuguese second tier and hosted Celtic in Leiria, 60 miles away from their home town. Hoops fans formed the vast majority of the 4,971 crowd. But the hosts started the game three points ahead of Celtic after wins over Lillestrøm and Ararat-Armenia, and they had taken the lead against Sunderland before the Premier League side netted a stoppage-time winner.
The lead-up to Marseille against Levski Sofia was marred by incidents in the stands between supporters, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. Several Marseille fans ran from the stand about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski supporters were gathered.
Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. “Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder,” the Marseille police prefecture said. Six others were treated on site for various wounds. The home team went on to win the game 1-0 thanks to a first-half Amine Gouiri penalty.
Ruben Amorim’s Milan gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos.
Milan were facing another huge blow to their bid to reach the knockout phase when they were trailing to a Mike Maignan own goal and Jota Silva’s 49th-minute strike. Omari Hutchinson’s brilliant solo goal gave Milan a lifeline, and the winger then set up Alphadjo Cissé to equalise in the 63rd minute.
Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira’s injury-time fourth.
Juventus shrugged off an early scare to cruise past Cypriots Omonia Nicosia and move closer to confirming a top-eight place in the Europa League with a 4-1 win in Turin.
The Italian giants fell behind to a 15th-minute strike from Lubomir Satka but levelled through Andrea Cambiaso before further goals from Jeff Ekhator, Francisco Conceiçao and Jeremie Boga earned a comfortable win. Only Bournemouth sit above Juve in the table.
Bayer Leverkusen also remained in contention for automatic progression after second-half strikes from Malik Tillman and Jarell Quansah secured a 2-0 win at Dinamo Zagreb. Hoffenheim secured their second win in this season’s competition by beating Sturm Graz 3-1.

items.title: With World Cup qualification at stake, the USWNT has no excuses
items.summary:
The task for the U.S. women's national team is simple: one win and they're in for the 2027 Women's World Cup.
On paper, Concacaf's revamped qualification format looks even easier for the USWNT: As the region's top team and the FIFA No. 2-ranked team in the world, the USWNT faces El Salvador, the tea
items.text:
The task for the U.S. women's national team is simple: one win and they're in for the 2027 Women's World Cup.
On paper, Concacaf's revamped qualification format looks even easier for the USWNT: As the region's top team and the FIFA No. 2-ranked team in the world, the USWNT faces El Salvador, the team ranked No. 78 in the world, in the tournament quarterfinal on Friday in Mansfield, Texas.
Naturally, USWNT head coach Emma Hayes is not taking the bait.
"For us as a whole, Concacaf is a very different competition," Hayes told reporters on Saturday in Washington, D.C. "... These are the games where you say to yourself, 'Oh, you know, this is an easier opponent.' Let me be clear about this: This will be a very, very tough game. You have to prepare in the right way possible, and I will absolutely be making sure our group is switched on when they come in. It's really important."
Concacaf simplified its final phase of qualifying to be a single-elimination tournament after FIFA reduced the number of international match windows. The four winners of the quarterfinals on Friday and Saturday will advance to the 2027 World Cup, while the losers will go into a play-in bracket to advance to the global playoff. In other words: if the U.S. advances vs. El Salvador on Friday, the rest of the Concacaf tournament doesn't matter -- the USA's World Cup spot will have been clinched.
With all due respect to the rest of the field, the Americans' toughest opponent could be themselves.
Health and fatigue are factors. Eighteen of the 23 players on the USWNT roster for qualifying compete in the NWSL, which just wrapped up its grueling eight-months season on Saturday. Forward Trinity Rodman has already been removed from the World Cup qualifying roster after sustaining a shoulder injury in the opening minutes of the Washington Spirit's 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current in the NWSL Championship.
Without a doubt, there are other U.S. players carrying knocks or heavy legs following the NWSL season. Several of them, like midfielder Rose Lavelle, played more limited roles in the NWSL playoffs as they managed health issues. They must all quickly switch from club to international duties.
"Get used to it -- that's the realities of it," Hayes said.
And, as usual, this FIFA window comes immediately after the NWSL Championship -- except this time it for World Cup qualifying, not a set of friendlies like in previous years.
"There is no such thing as a friendly," Hayes said when asked about the difference in approach to this window. "It's a terrible term. They need to get rid of it. Every game is a competitive game, and if you don't train like it's your World Cup final and play games like that, how can you expect to perform at that level? For me, it's no different than the other games that we play, except we have the opportunity to qualify for something. That's the only difference."
In theory, Concacaf's updated qualifying format is more difficult. Single-elimination knockout games typically give less talented teams a greater chance at an upset as opposed to round-robin or group-stage tournaments in which teams need consistent results to advance.
Concacaf has reverted from its previous format ahead of the 2023 World Cup, when two groups of four played in the 100-degree daily heat of Monterrey, Mexico, for four automatic bids and two berths in FIFA's global playoff. The outcome was thrilling and entertaining by the standards of Concacaf tournaments: Concacaf ultimately maxed out its potential World Cup berths at six (and Jamaica was the most impressive member nation at the 2026 World Cup), and somehow hosts Mexico were one of the two teams that did not advance at all.
However, the changes to FIFA's international calendar and fixture congestion led to another simplified, single-elimination tournament. Concacaf created more meaningful games in the buildup to the final stage of qualifying, to develop teams and provide more meaningful games of consequence for more teams. Canada and the U.S. are joined by the six group-stage winners, including El Salvador, in the quarterfinals.
The four winners of the quarterfinals will advance to the 2027 World Cup, while the losers will go into a play-in bracket to advance to the global playoff. Three teams will also qualify for the 2028 Olympics alongside the U.S., who will host the Games.
The reality for the USWNT is that qualifying is almost always a formality. The only time that was not true was 16 years ago, when the U.S. women lost a Concacaf semifinal to Mexico in Cancun in the biggest upset in program history. The Americans were ranked No. 1 in the world but had to then go beat Italy in a two-leg playoff to qualify as the 16th and final team for the 2011 World Cup.
Those stories -- the raucous crowd in Mexico, Abby Wambach getting her head stapled in the final minutes of the game, a young Alex Morgan saving the U.S. in the first leg in Italy -- were passed on across generations of players so that the mistake would not be repeated.
El Salvador is even less likely to pull off an upset than that talented Mexico team from 16 years ago.
Friday's quarterfinal will be played in suburban Dallas, for one. Poorly promoted Concacaf games don't have the crowds of U.S. Soccer-hosted or FIFA-hosted ones, but the home field advantage will go to the U.S., if anyone.
El Salvador have their own problems, too. The team was in turmoil a month ago when its coach, Eric Acuña, made comments to reporters questioning his players' commitment and threatening to revoke their basic rights to do things like getting coffee during training camp. Acuña also publicly criticized his players, who responded strongly to rebuke their coach.
The El Salvadorian federation released a statement condemning Acuña's comments and supporting the players, but the coach remains in charge for qualifying.
El Salvador's federation released a statement on Tuesday saying that the 23 players on the World Cup qualifying roster will share a $1 milli

items.title: How USWNT can qualify for World Cup, matchups, format
items.summary:
The 2027 Women's World Cup is approaching quickly, but there are still plenty of spots up for grabs in the sport's biggest tournament.
Four of those places will be decided at the Concacaf W Championship, where the United States, Canada and Mexico are among the participating teams.
Here's everything
items.text:
The 2027 Women's World Cup is approaching quickly, but there are still plenty of spots up for grabs in the sport's biggest tournament.
Four of those places will be decided at the Concacaf W Championship, where the United States, Canada and Mexico are among the participating teams.
Here's everything you need to know about the upcoming tournament.
- How teams can qualify for 2027 Women's World Cup
When is the Concacaf W Championship?
The tournament begins Nov. 27 and concludes with the final on Dec. 5. All matches will take place in Houston and Mansfield, Texas.
What is the format?
The Concacaf W Championship is essentially a straight knockout tournament between eight qualifying teams. (The two highest-ranked teams in the FIFA Women's World Ranking as of Aug. 7 -- the United States and Canada -- earned safe passage to the W Championship, while the remaining teams had to win their groups in the qualifying round.)
The teams were seeded according to their FIFA ranking and placed in a bracket, with the No. 1 seed facing No. 8, No. 2 paired with No. 7, and so on. Winners in the quarterfinals advance to the semifinals, and the winning semifinal teams will contest the final.
Here are the matchups in the quarterfinal round:
No. 1 United States vs. No. 8 El Salvador (Nov. 27, 8:30 p.m. ET)
No. 4 Jamaica vs. No. 5 Costa Rica (Nov. 27, 5 p.m. ET)
No. 2 Canada vs. No. 7 Panama (Nov. 28, 1 p.m. ET)
No. 3 Mexico vs. No. 6 Haiti (Nov. 28, 4:30 p.m. ET)
How do teams qualify for the Women's World Cup?
Quite simply, the four teams that win in the quarterfinals will qualify for the Women's World Cup. For the U.S. women, that means a win against El Salvador on Nov. 27 will send them through to the World Cup.
If a team loses in the quarterfinals, can they still qualify?
Yes -- the losing teams will compete in play-in matches for the interconfederation playoffs, which conclude in February. Those playoffs will determine the final qualifiers for the World Cup.
Which teams are the favorites to win it all?
The United States remains the powerhouse in Concacaf. The winner in nine of the past 11 editions of this tournament (as well as four-time World Cup champions), coach Emma Hayes' team is firmly expected to steamroll its way to the final.
Canada might have something to say about that, though. Its FIFA ranking of ninth signals the threat they pose; boasting young stars such as Arsenal's Olivia Smith and veterans Jessie Fleming and Kadeisha Buchanan, Canada is capable of pushing the U.S. to the limit.
Who are the USWNT players to watch?
The United States' 51-player preliminary roster for the tournament was trimmed down to 23 and finalized on Nov. 18. Forwards Trinity Rodman, Mallory Swanson and Sophia Wilson are among the players hoping to get on the scoresheet, while experienced midfielders Rose Lavelle and Lindsey Heaps will look to control the center of the pitch.
OL Lyonnes' Lily Yohannes could also make a big impact. The highly regarded 19-year-old midfielder scored a stunning strike from long range in the UEFA Women's Champions League back in October.
One notable player who wasn't named to the team is Chelsea center back Naomi Girma, who has been out with a muscle injury since early October.

items.summary:

Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after staging a 10-man fightback to join a select band of teams to win their first five European games.
The Cherries trailed 1-0 to Iago Aspas' goal at Celta Vigo,
items.text:
Bournemouth 'allowed to dream' as fans book Europa League final hotels
- Published
Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after staging a 10-man fightback to join a select band of teams to win their first five European games.
The Cherries trailed 1-0 to Iago Aspas' goal at Celta Vigo, and then went down to 10 men midway through the first half when Bafode Diakite was sent off.
But second-half goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan gave the Cherries a 10th consecutive win in all competitions, extending their club record run.
Bournemouth are only the third side to win each of their first five European matches (excluding qualifiers and including the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup), after Nuremberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73.
They top this season's table as the only club to win five out of five - and are closing in on a top-eight spot, which would mean they skip a play-off round and go straight into the last 16.
Some fans have told the BBC they have already booked hotels in Frankfurt for the final on 26 May.
As supporters sang about reaching that game, midfielder Alex Scott was asked for his thoughts on TNT Sports.
"Of course that's our dream. When you grow up wanting to be a footballer you dream of winning trophies," Scott said.
"Where this club has come from to where it is now, full credit to everyone who has built it.
"For players, it's a dream to be on the pitch playing for this club. We have still got wins to get to qualify into the top eight, and from there all focus is on pushing forward and hopefully we can go on and win it."
'We were just relentless'
The Cherries are in unprecedented times, with their biggest trophy to date being when they won the second-tier Championship in 2014-15.
In terms of cups, they won the 1983–84 Associate Members' Cup - which later became the EFL Trophy.
Head coach Marco Rose, who replaced Andoni Iraola in the summer, said: "It's always allowed to dream.
"If you get a competition like this you want to achieve the best possible thing. We know it's far away to go. Many games. Now it's about getting into the top eight to avoid more games and then we can see step by step."
As well as just winning their games, Bournemouth are firing in the goals. They have netted at least twice in each match during this 10-game winning run.
And they are the first side to score at least twice in each of their first five matches in Europe since Queens Park Rangers in 1976.
The win on Thursday was made even more impressive by the fact they contested 75% of the game with 10 men.
It came days after Manchester United seemed to implode after an early red card against Liverpool, losing 4-0.
Former England manager Glenn Hoddle said on TNT: "They have deserved this result. They've played beautifully with 10 men - probably as good as I've seen a team play defensively and with the ball.
"I've not seen a team go down to 10 men for so long and dictate a game and deserve to win the game. They were absolutely brilliant."
Cherries boss Rose told BBC Radio Solent: "What a team, what a spirit, what an energy.
"I said to Ty [Tyler Adams] sometimes it's not about tactics and formations and stuff like this. [David] Brooks did a great job when we got one player less - he played right defender like he played it for 10 years. We changed in the right moment. Everyone did his job on a really high level.
"We were just relentless and we never stopped to believe in this win and that's why big, big, big congratulations to the team.
"You feel if you're one player down that it's a difficult night, but to handle a difficult night like this, it just shows the character of the team and of the whole group."
The coach's belief in what they are doing filters through to the players.
Amine Adli, who set up the equaliser, told the BBC: "At half-time, everyone still believed we can turn the game in our way and this is what happened.
"Everyone was like 'guys we can make it, we have to believe. If we score the game can change.'"
Earlier this month, the attacking midfielder said he saw a lot of similarities to the Bayer Leverkusen team he was part of in 2023-24.
That is not a bad comparison, considering they went unbeaten to win the domestic double, as well as reaching the Europa League final.
So who can blame the Cherries for dreaming?

Jagiellonia Bialystok’s head coach, Adrian Siemieniec claimed this trip to Wearside to face Premier League opposition represented one of the biggest highlights of a career that has already seen him celebrate a Polish title.
His players did everything to guarantee it was not an anticlimax as they del
items.text:
Jagiellonia Bialystok’s head coach, Adrian Siemieniec claimed this trip to Wearside to face Premier League opposition represented one of the biggest highlights of a career that has already seen him celebrate a Polish title.
His players did everything to guarantee it was not an anticlimax as they delighted in highlighting Sunderland’s struggles in front of goal courtesy of some intelligent defending. Along the way they also responded to falling behind with an almost immediate equaliser and forced Robin Roefs into the evening’s more taxing saves.
The city of Bialystok lies in eastern Poland, close to the Belarusian and Lithuanian borders but the arduous journey to north-east England was not responsible for the lack of Jagiellonia fans inside the Stadium of Light.
Instead visiting supporters were banned from making the trip by Uefa as punishment for misbehaviour at Levski Sofia earlier this season. Their absence contributed to a strangely flat atmosphere on a brutally cold Wearside night. Although a reasonably strong Sunderland starting XI were largely dominant they struggled to undo Jagiellonia’s indefatigable defence.
Granted Enzo Le Fée contributed some lovely touches and often looked the best player on the pitch but Régis Le Bris’s playmaker needed support and it seemed in scant supply. When Le Fée cued up Nilson Angulo a goal seemed inevitable but a splendid visiting block served as a reminder that Jagiellonia appeared determined to play in the spirit of their founders – soldiers from the 42nd infantry regiment of the Polish army.
At least Malick Fofana’s confidence should have been boosted by a superbly calibrated left foot shot that forced a stellar save from Slawomir Abramowicz. The Belgium winger has struggled since arriving from Lyon in a £30m summer deadline day move but here was a hint – albeit fairly isolated – of the potential that led Sunderland to engage in an extraordinary transfer tug of war with Crystal Palace before eventually winning his signature.
Although Robin Roefs was forced into just one significant first-half save – to repel Kajetan Szmyt’s free-kick – Omar Alderete’s struggles this season continued in the shape of an error-strewn performance. In mitigation perhaps the centre-half – excellent last season – was struggling with an injury as, shortly before half-time, he signalled to the bench that he needed to come off and was replaced by Luke O’Nien.
Le Bris introduced two more new faces at the outset of the second period as, with Sunday’s all important home Premier League game with Tottenham looming, he offered Noah Sadiki and Trai Hume rests, sending Jules Ahoka and Thomas Meunier on in their place. The newcomers were soon celebrating. When Le Fée crossed incisively from the right Timur Tutierov was just onside and the young Ukrainian striker delighted in heading Sunderland in front from point black range.
That lead did not last long. Errors on the part of Ahoka and then, most significantly, Reinildo’s panicked, failed, attempted back pass left Kamil Jozwiak free to round Roefs and sweep an imperious equalising shot into the back of the net.
The need to keep Le Fée’s legs reasonably fresh for Spurs saw the Frenchman replaced by Chemsdine Talbi. By then Roefs had made an excellent save to deny Jozwiak a second goal after another mistake from the immensely promising yet deeply inexperienced Ahoka and the simmering disgruntlement of Sunderland fans was becoming audible.
When visiting substitute Jesús Imaz subsequently directed an extremely presentable chance straight at Roefs there was a sense calamity had been averted. Even so, A smattering of boos greeted the final whistle as a frowning Le Bris’s hopes of avoiding the playoffs and qualifying automatically for the knockout phase receded.

items.title: Paris Fury retracts Tyson schizophrenia claim

Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband has been diagnosed with schizophrenia
Paris Fury says Tyson did not receive a diagnosis of schizophrenia; Netflix documentary has now been updated; The British Boxing Board of Control indicated it would look into comments about a sc
items.text:
Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband has been diagnosed with schizophrenia
Paris Fury says Tyson did not receive a diagnosis of schizophrenia; Netflix documentary has now been updated; The British Boxing Board of Control indicated it would look into comments about a schizophrenia diagnosis and could deny Fury a licence to face Anthony Joshua on December 11
Thursday 26 November 2026 23:20, UK
Paris Fury has retracted her claim that husband Tyson Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia.
A new Netflix documentary explores Tyson Fury's experiences of depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder, which became particularly acute after his unified heavyweight championship victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.
Paris Fury made the comments about schizophrenia in an initial version of the documentary. Netflix said it has worked to "update" the footage in light of her clarification.
She has now said: "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic'. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn't have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.
"Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. I'm so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we've received as a family."
Earlier on Thursday, the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBoC) indicated that it was investigating the comments and could deny Fury a licence to face Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11 if he was deemed unfit to fight.
Sky Sports News has contacted the BBBoC to clarify if an investigation is ongoing after Paris Fury's retraction.
A spokesperson for Netflix said: "Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson's official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch."
After his victory over Klitschko, Fury revealed he had struggled with drug and alcohol addiction and had gained weight.
He was admitted to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack, and revealed that while in hospital he had heard voices in his head.
"Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury said during the Netflix documentary.
"It was like a living version of the pits of hell.
"I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.
"The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London. She asked me a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder."
The NHS says schizophrenia is a long-term mental health illness that is a form of psychosis.
Those suffering from the condition may, at times, be unable to distinguish their own thoughts from reality. Symptoms can include hallucinations and delusions.
The NHS describes bipolar disorder as a mental health issue where a person can experience extreme changes in their mood.
If you've been affected by anything discussed in this article, support is available; please visit Sky Viewer Support.
If you are worried about your mental health, get advice and support through your GP or call the NHS on 111.
Find free, confidential support through:
- Samaritans: Call 116 123 (available 24/7)
- SHOUT: Text 85258 (available 24/7)

items.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
items.summary: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s came 17 minutes from time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory was turn
items.text:
Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s came 17 minutes from time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory was turned on its head after Jon Martin was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser.
The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none. The Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step despite Yéremy Pino’s missed penalty in injury time after the outstanding Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory.
Frank had urged the Palace supporters ensure the atmosphere was “through the roof” for his home debut and he immediately made a beeline for the Holmesdale Road End after emerging from the tunnel. Almost all of his squad – including the two substitute goalkeepers – had spent a substantial part of the warm-up practising defending set pieces so there was no doubt where the priorities lay. But the Palace manager didn’t look amused when Mamadou Sarr was inches away from connecting with a free-kick in the second minute as the visitors served warning of the threat they posed.
Sociedad have struggled in this competition despite a promising start to their La Liga campaign and it was a surprise to see Pellegrino Matarazzo match Frank’s 4-4-2 formation in what felt like something of a throwback to the mid 1990s. With Adam Wharton suspended after his red card against Hoffenheim, Palace found it very difficult to escape their press as Mateta and Eddie Nketiah were forced to feed off whatever scraps that came their way.
Ben Chilwell looked unsettled by the pace of Héctor Fort, the former Barcelona right-back, and Sociedad began to target the former England defender’s left flank. Mikel Oyarzabal should have done much better when he was picked out by the lively Arsen Zakharyan.
Not for the first time, Palace had Henderson to thank for keeping the scores level when Zakharyan was given far too much time and space by Chilwell. The Russian picked out Goncalo Guedes and his shot was parried away to safety. The former Wolves forward tried his luck again soon after and once more Henderson was equal to his effort. The Palace captain could not hide his emotions as he rightly questioned why their opponents were being afforded so much space. Mateta had to wait until the final minute of the first half for a sighter and the France striker could only nod over from a long Chris Richards throw.
Henderson was called into action twice inside the opening six minutes of the second half as Sociedad smelled blood. Oyarzabal should have rounded off a lightning-quick break downfield but could only shoot straight at the England goalkeeper before Jon Gorrotxategi was denied from the edge of the area. With his side struggling to gain a foothold, Frank abandoned his experiment with Nketiah and brought on Dwight McNeil to try to give Chilwell a helping hand. Yet it was down Palace’s left flank that Sociedad finally found the breakthrough when Sarr touched home Job Ochieng’s cros
To their credit, Palace’s response was immediate. Disasi won a header from another long throw and Martin hauled down Mateta as he was about to score, earning a second yellow card. Mateta dispatched the spot kick with aplomb and only a desperate goalline clearance from Sarr denied Kamada. Frank went for broke by throwing on Jorgen Strand Larsen and his gamble paid off when the Norway striker’s attempted overhead kick presented McNeil with the easiest of opportunities to lift the gloom in these parts.

Report from the Europa League clash between Torreense and Celtic at Campo Manuel Marques; Javi Vazquez' own-goal put Celtic in front; Dany Jean levelled before the break; substitute Camilo Duran headed in a late winner for the Hoops; Martin O'Neill's side are up to 25th
Thursday 26 November 2026 22:55, UK
Camilo Duran came off the bench to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive with a vital win against Torreense.
The Colombian striker peeled away to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest, guiding a downward header into the net in the 85th minute.
Duran's 15th goal of the season secured a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and moved Celtic on to six points in the Europa League. His latest decisive contribution follows a match-winning double off the bench in the Hoops' comeback victory over Besiktas last time out.
- Teams | Stats | Europa League fixtures and results
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Celtic games with no contract📺
Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vazquez turned Jota's cross into his own net, with Yang Hyun-jun lurking behind him.
However, the Portuguese Cup winners hit back 10 minutes later after some hesitant defending from the visitors. Alex Alfaro rattled the crossbar with a 22-yard effort, but neither Kieran Tierney nor Colby Donovan could deal with the resulting loose balls, allowing Haiti international Dany Jean to volley home the equaliser.
Celtic dominated possession after the break but struggled to create clear-cut opportunities until Duran's late intervention secured all three points.
The Hoops' attention now turns to Hearts on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, as they look to remain top of the Scottish Premiership.
Their next Europa League match is away to Omonia Nicosia on December 10.
Key moments from Campo Manuel Marques
2: CLOSE! Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain sends in a corner, it's flicked on by Liam Scales but Hyun-jun Yang can't knock the ball in before it's cleared.
9: GOAL CELTIC! Javi Vazquez tries to clear Jota's cross but turns it into his own net.
19: GOAL TORREENSE! Alex Alfaro's effort rattles the underside of the bar, Celtic fail to make a clearance and Dany Jean fires in the equaliser.
33: SAVE! Jota's powerful strike is pushed over the bar by Adriel.
36: OFF THE LINE! More awful defending from Celtic, but Liam Scales manages to head the ball clear.
47: SAVE! Jota tries to chip the ball over the goalkeeper but he manages to pluck the ball out of the air.
53: BLOCK! Jota is continuing to cause problems for the hosts as he sends in a cross for Kieran Tierney, which is headed behind.
61: CLOSE! Jean looks to squeeze in a shot at the near post, but it's just wide.
69: CHANCE! A misplaced pass from Oliver Sorensen lets Musa Drammeh get a shot away. Thankfully for Celtic it's wide.
70: LET OFF FOR CELTIC! Trouble at the back again gives Drammeh space to get a shot away, but the former Hearts striker is inches wide.
84: GOAL CELTIC! Camilo Duran rises at the back post to head in James Forrest's cross. Celtic are back ahead.
O'Neill: 'From an almost impossible position, we have hope'
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill on TNT Sports:
"I'm just delighted to have won, it keeps us going if nothing else. We've got six points on the board and we've still a couple of games to go.
"From an almost impossible position, having lost the first three games, we've given ourselves some hope.
"Three points tonight were of vital importance. There's lots we can still do to improve our game."
Asked about Camilo Duran, he added: "He's just a magnificent footballer.
"15 goals and we're not into December, he's been flying. He's a terrific player, and that's two games he's come up big for us."
Jota 'enjoying life' as he returns to best
Celtic winger Jota speaking to TNT Sports after his first European appearance for almost two years:
"It was a long road and I did my maximum to be as fit as possible.
"Right now, it's all about enjoying life. No expectations, just be professional and having the responsibility of being a Celtic player.
"It wasn't easy. I think we just had to stick with our plan and in the end it worked out, that's the most important thing.
"We must believe [Celtic can qualify]. Every game is a different battle, we know what to do."

Thursday 26 November 2026 22:13, UK
Thomas Frank earned his first win as Crystal Palace manager, coming from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League.
The Dane lost his opening game to Coventry at the weekend, but saw the heart and fight he will need from his side as they picked up their second win in the competition this season.
For 70 minutes, Sociedad dominated at Selhurst Park, with Dean Henderson needed to make a string of saves. They finally made the breakthrough when Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr tapped home from Job Ochieng's cross.

But the game turned out of nowhere as Crystal Palace were awarded a penalty and Jon Martin was sent off. He picked up a second yellow card for holding Jean-Philippe Mateta round the middle, with the striker expertly dispatching the spot kick to level for the Eagles.
The confidence surged in the hosts - backed by the famous atmosphere at Selhurst Park - and it was a well-worked second that put them ahead.
Yeremy Pino's cross was cleared to Jorgen Strand Larsen at the back post, who hit an overhead kick. It wasn't on target, but it did bobble into the six-yard box for the incoming Dwight McNeill, who slid to poke home.
Crystal Palace could have wrapped up the points in a topsy-turvy end after they were awarded another penalty. Carlos Soler was penalised for handball, but Pino's effort was well-saved by Unai Marrero.

items.title: AI made self-hosting fun again
items.summary:
AI made self-hosting fun again
I’ve been self-hosting things for many years. There were times when I was quite enthusiastic about it, constantly trying out new software and tinkering with my infrastructure. But at some point, that enthusiasm faded a bit.
I never really stopped self-hosting, but I be
items.text:
AI made self-hosting fun again
I’ve been self-hosting things for many years. There were times when I was quite enthusiastic about it, constantly trying out new software and tinkering with my infrastructure. But at some point, that enthusiasm faded a bit.
I never really stopped self-hosting, but I became less inclined to experiment with new things. Maintaining what I already had running was enough for me.
Over the last few months, however, I’ve found myself getting increasingly excited about self-hosting again. And, somewhat ironically, AI is a big reason for that.
Less friction
Most of my infrastructure configuration lives in Git repositories, mainly in the form of Docker Compose files, scripts, and other configuration files. This makes it possible to use AI coding agents to work on my infrastructure in much the same way as they would work on any other software project.
Whenever I want to try a new service, adjust an existing configuration, or automate something, I can now do so with considerably less effort.
In the past, I would sometimes put off certain changes simply because I didn’t feel like spending an evening reading changelogs and documentation or troubleshooting issues. It’s not that I couldn’t have done these things before. But often, the amount of effort required just wasn’t worth it to me.
Now, even relatively spontaneous ideas often end up becoming reality.
Trying things I always found interesting
There are also technologies that I’ve always found interesting but never felt knowledgeable enough about to really make use of them.
NixOS is a good example. I’ve always liked the idea of declaratively configuring an entire system; I even used it on my laptop during my Linux honeymoon phase. But getting everything configured the way I wanted was quite a hurdle. With the help of AI, I’m now making much more extensive use of NixOS on my home server.
For my VPS infrastructure, I’ve also started building my own Debian-based bootc image (after thinking about it for some time).
Having my entire operating system configuration defined in a Git repository and automatically building a bootable container image from it is something I find really cool. But it’s also something I probably wouldn’t have invested enough time in to get working on my own before. Even with the help of AI, it still took me half a day when I set it up a few months ago. Without AI, it would probably have taken me at least a week.
AI makes experimenting with unfamiliar technologies much more approachable. I don’t necessarily need to understand every little detail before I can get started. I can learn about things along the way, ask questions, and gradually improve my configurations.
Automating almost everything
Something I’ve also finally managed to do is automate most of the build, update, and deployment processes for my infrastructure.
A lot of the work involved in self-hosting isn’t particularly exciting. Keeping track of new releases, updating container image tags, building images, and deploying configuration changes are all things that need to be done regularly.
I still remember what updating a service used to look like: bumping the version and adjusting the Docker Compose file on my laptop, pushing the changes to the Git remote, SSHing into the server, pulling the changes, and finally deploying them. Now, a single Git push is enough. If a push is even necessary.
With Renovate, I no longer need to actively keep track of most software updates. It creates pull requests for me, and often, all I need to do is review and merge them. I can even do that on my phone while sitting on the sofa.
Pushing changes or merging a pull request triggers the corresponding GitHub Actions or Forgejo Actions workflows, which take care of building and deploying everything.
Of course, there’s nothing particularly groundbreaking about any of this. DevOps has been around for a long time, and none of these automation tools require AI. But AI has helped me put all these pieces together in a way that I previously never quite got around to doing.
And the nice thing about automating these tasks is that the benefits extend well beyond the initial setup. I now have less tedious work to do every time I want to change something or update a service.
Back to more powerful hardware
As I’ve started hosting more things again, I’ve also moved more of my services from my VPS to my home server.
For a while, I was using an HP t640 thin client as my home server. However, with more things I wanted to run, I decided to switch back to my ASRock DeskMini A300, which had been sitting unused for some time. I’m thinking about repurposing the t640 as a “router on a stick”, though.
I even took the opportunity to upgrade its CPU from an AMD Ryzen 5 2400G to a Ryzen 5 PRO 4650G and replaced the stock AMD cooler with a quieter Noctua cooler. Noise was the main reason I switched to the t640 in the first place.
It’s nice to put some hardware I already owned back to use rather than buying an entirely new machine. I also managed to get both the CPU and the cooler for a good price through a classifieds site.
Having some additional computing power available gives me more room to experiment. And there’s something quite satisfying about having a small box at home running a growing collection of services that I use in my everyday life.
Building my own tools
But it’s not just about self-hosting existing software. AI has also changed how I approach problems for which there isn’t an existing piece of software that does exactly what I want.
Previously, I would often spend quite some time searching for a suitable open-source project, comparing different alternatives, and figuring out how to make one of them work for my particular use case.
These days, for smaller problems, building my own solution has become a much more attractive option.
I’ve recently built tools to automatically download invoices, e-papers or Linux ISOs.
I can build (or have AI build) these tools in Go, my preferred pr

items.text:
Fury vs Joshua undercard: Martin Bakole insists late-notice Deontay Wilder fight won't be like Joseph Parker loss
In his first interview since agreeing to step in to fight Deontay Wilder, Martin Bakole explains his decision and why he believes this late-notice assignment will be very different from when he flew in to fight Joseph Parker; Bakole says victory will lead him to a world title shot
Thursday 26 November 2026 22:06, UK
Martin Bakole explained his decision to step in as a replacement opponent for Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard next month.
After Jai Opetaia withdrew from his December 11 bout with former heavyweight world champion Wilder, Bakole came in to take his place on the Principality Stadium bill.
He insists it is a very different scenario to his short-notice assignment against Joseph Parker last year.
Bakole came in to box Parker for the WBO Interim title, landing in Riyadh just a day before the fight. Parker promptly put him down heavily and stopped him in their second round.
For this fight with Wilder though he's had more warning. He was training in Las Vegas to box on the same bill, albeit originally for a much lower-level opponent.
"When I heard Wilder doesn't have an opponent, his opponent cancelled, they proposed me and I said why not? I'm ready to give a big fight," Bakole told Sky Sports. "Why not jump from a comeback fight to a big fight?
"I was surprised they mentioned my name and I said yes," he added. "I'm ready to come back again because I want to take over now the heavyweight division.
"I don't see Deontay beating me. He doesn't have the strength I have.
"I don't see any danger because I like danger, I like to impose myself.
"I'm ready and prepared for him."
That wasn't the case for Parker when he took that fight. "I was out in the Congo on holiday, I jumped in," Bakole said.
"In that fight I was giving Joseph Parker a hard time in the first round but because I was not fit and my head was not moving, he landed a punch. But I don't regret that fight. It's just part of my story.
"That was something to save the card."
While Bakole has been training in Las Vegas, he will still have long-time coach Billy Nelson in his corner for the fight.
"I came here to learn something new. I was getting ready for everyone," Bakole said. "Everything has changed [with his preparation], conditioning, nutrition."
He believes victory over Wilder will lead him to a world title shot next year.
"Of course," Bakole said. "That's why I wanted to change everything because I know next year, with my team, with His Excellency's [Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh] help, I will get a world title next year."

items.title: Bears stun Lions with TD in final seconds of NFL Thanksgiving epic
items.summary:
NFL: Chicago Bears stun Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving with game-winning touchdown in final three seconds
Detroit Lions lead for 53 minutes and 31 seconds, stretching their advantage to 11 points midway through final quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs' third TD from 70 yards out; Rome Odunze scores twice, in
items.text:
NFL: Chicago Bears stun Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving with game-winning touchdown in final three seconds
Detroit Lions lead for 53 minutes and 31 seconds, stretching their advantage to 11 points midway through final quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs' third TD from 70 yards out; Rome Odunze scores twice, including game-winner, to clinch Chicago Bears comeback that secures top spot in NFC North
Thursday 26 November 2026 22:08, UK
The Chicago Bears scored the game-winning touchdown with just three seconds remaining to secure a stunning 39-35 comeback win over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving and claim first place in the NFC North.
Rome Odunze's second TD - a sensational toe-tap grab in the back of the end zone - clinched the victory and deny Detroit, who had led by 11 earlier in the fourth quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs ran in his third score of the game from 70 yards out.
Chicago's lead secured right at the death was the first lead change in a game they've been involved with since they trailed the Carolina Panthers 7-0 in the first quarter of their opening game of the season. They had trailed the Lions for 53 minutes and 31 seconds of this match.
- How to watch NFL Thanksgiving week live on Sky Sports
- Jay-Z picks himself to headline Super Bowl half-time show
- Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW
The Bears' dramatic win nudges them into solo first in the fiercely-fought NFC North, at 9-2 on the season, while the Lions drop to 8-3 with a first loss in seven.
It also improves Chicago's record in the division to 1-2, with Detroit now 2-1, which could prove crucial should any potential playoff tiebreakers be necessary to separate the two teams - who meet again on the penultimate week of the season - or the Minnesota Vikings (7-3) and Green Bay Packers (6-5).
The game was initially slow to ignite, with only a Lions field goal to show from the first quarter, before Gibbs' first score to start the second lit the blue touchpaper.
The Lions continued to lead thereafter, until the Bears came roaring back in the final quarter. Caleb Williams firstly located Odunze deep down the field for a 41-yard TD, the QB ran in the resulting two-point play to cut the score to three, before Jared Goff threw an interception on the next series.
Chicago turned the ball over on downs, failing to convert on 4th and 3 just inside Detroit territory, but they got the ball back with just over two minutes to go, and this time marched down the field before Williams linked up with Odunze again for the game winner with seconds remaining.
Williams finished with 345 yards passing and those two scoring strikes to Odunze, while Bears running back D'Andre Swift had 162 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown. Gibbs had 20 carries for a massive 205 yards and three TDs for the Lions but it didn't prove to be enough.
Stats leaders
Bears:
- Passing: Caleb Williams, 30/44, 345 yards, 2 TDs
- Rushing: D'Andre Swift, 9 carries, 65 yards, 1 TD
- Receiving: D'Andre Swift, 7 catches, 97 yards
- Rome Odunze, 6 catches, 87 yards, 2 TDs
Lions:
- Passing: Jared Goff, 25/36, 313 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT
- Rushing: Jahmyr Gibbs, 21 carries, 205 yards, 3 TDs
- Receiving: Amon-Ra St. Brown, 7 catches, 146 yards
How the Bears roared back on Thanksgiving
After the Lions' first quarter field goal, they failed to add further points on the back of a Colston Loveland fumble, but they would find the end zone early in the second - Gibbs from down at the goal line - as the Bears offense was slow to fire.
Chicago finally sparked into life in the second and tied the game up at 10-10 with the first of two Kyle Monangai scores.
Detroit were back in front by the half, up 19-10, after a bizarre sequence saw them first awarded a safety as a Bears player deliberately batted a fumbled football out of the end zone, before Goff found Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard TD.
A second Gibbs touchdown was sandwiched in between scores for Monangai and Swift in the third quarter, while Jake Bates' second field goal put the Lions 29-24 up early in the fourth.
Gibbs only added to that advantage as he completed his hat-trick of TDs with the best of the bunch, breaking loose from 70 yards out but the game was far from over, with Willams and Odunze answering back almost immediately.
After Chicago failed to capitalise on Goff's interception, Detroit missed the chance to ice the game when opting against a 50-yard field goal try as they went for it on 4th and 4 from the Bears 33-yard-line.
Stopped short, Chicago got the ball back to pave the way for Williams and Odunze's dramatic, game-winning connection in the closing seconds.

items.title: Kamil Khan Mumtaz: Pakistani architect, admired at home, almost invisible abroad
items.summary:

items.text:
Traditional architecture is alive and well in Lahore. A photo essay of Kamil Khan Mumtaz’s greatest works.
Some years ago, my colleague Ben Southwood sent me a handful of grainy online pictures showing some recent buildings in Pakistan. I was struck by the assurance of the designs and the quality of the materials, craftsmanship, and detailing. They seemed to be the work of one Kamil Khan Mumtaz, a Pakistani architect widely admired in his home country but almost invisible abroad. I wondered whether Mumtaz might be the world’s best architect, overlooked because global architecture magazines rarely do photoshoots in Lahore. Last year, I met his assistant Sohaib Ahmed at a conference and immediately entreated him to send Works in Progress any photographs he had of the practice’s work. With Mumtaz’s support, Sohaib prepared a portfolio for us, most of it never before seen outside Pakistan.
Kamil Khan Mumtaz was born in Calcutta in 1939 and grew up in what became Pakistan, taking British A-levels at Lahore’s elite Aitchison College. He then moved to London to study at the Architectural Association. Although he had never previously left South Asia, Mumtaz immediately felt at home in England. ‘It seemed completely familiar. I didn’t feel like a stranger at all’, he recalled in an interview with the historian Chris Moffat. ‘I think this is because of having been brought up on essentially English books, in English schools. So, the whole thing was like, “I know this place”.’ Mumtaz enjoyed his studies at the Architectural Association, which taught a standard modernist approach that Mumtaz accepted unquestioningly: ‘I just simply took it hook, line and sinker, and swallowed the whole thing.’
Mumtaz returned to Pakistan in 1966 and began practicing as an architect. At around the same time, he became a communist activist, on account of which he was twice imprisoned by the military dictatorship. He remained resolutely modernist, although he acquired special interest in adapting modernism to the local climate and locally sourced building materials. He also became involved in architectural conservation. In the late 1970s, he prepared a report on the ancient Walled City of Lahore, highlighting its enormous heritage value and arguing for its preservation. ‘Our own bureaucrats only insisted that we should pull down the whole mess anyway, and build new, modern infrastructure and high-rise buildings, et cetera’, Mumtaz remembers. The Walled City was ultimately saved, and parts of it are now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Through the 1970s, Mumtaz began to question his approach. ‘I had this growing, nagging fear that I wasn’t communicating with my audience, as a visual artist or as an architect. This grew on me, almost like an obsession.’ In 1980, the Iranian architect Nader Ardalan gave him a copy of his book The Sense of Unity: The Sufi Tradition in Persian Architecture. Mumtaz initially paid no attention: ‘Flipping through it, I thought, “Oh yeah, this is traditional Iranian architecture, who cares!” I was totally uninterested.’ But eventually, frustrated by the sense that ‘I didn’t know the language of my own people’, he began to read. ‘From page one, it was mind-blowing. Absolutely. I thought, “My god, what have I been looking for? This is what I’ve been missing!” ... It shattered all of the beliefs I had, being a Marxist, a materialist, an atheist, a modernist.’
In the decades since, Mumtaz has worked to revive the older architectural traditions of Pakistan, and especially of Lahore, his home city. He has built a wide range of buildings, including homes, offices, mosques, and schools. His work has been received with warmth in Pakistan, though also with surprise. ‘I’ve found that there is a huge reservoir of desire, sympathy, and love for our traditional values, forms, architecture, and culture, altogether. But there’s a general kind of impression that these things can’t be done any more, there are no craftsmen who can do this.’
The loss of craft skills is a problem for traditional architecture everywhere. Some elements of traditional architecture have been prefabricated in factories for centuries, but even then, skill is needed for installation. Without skilled craftspeople, important details are often badly executed, making buildings look strange or clumsy. This problem also exists in Pakistan, but its later industrialization meant premodern craft traditions had not quite vanished when Mumtaz began work. Mumtaz recalled that, when searching for skilled craftsmen, ‘immediately, you come into contact with very small remnants of these families, hereditary craftsmen, and so the relationship grows.’
Mumtaz’s work has become steadily more technically sophisticated as he and his craftsmen have built up expertise. ‘Together we have been able to rediscover a number of the practices that had become lost. Certain types of brickwork, the flat dome, the muqarnas [ornamental vaults], many things like this that hadn’t been done. As they tell me, “This has not been done for 300 years!” So, it was a great experience, a voyage of discovery, so much that we learnt from each other.’
It is my great pleasure to introduce our readers to one of the most skilled and thoughtful architects working today.
Now in his mid-eighties, Mumtaz continues to build. ‘It does feel like you’ve set the foundations for an alternative approach to contemporary urban environments’, an interviewer recently suggested to him. ‘I’m just keeping my fingers crossed! No idea what will happen’, Mumtaz replied.
